articles.title: Havana, Caracas and Trump’s Unfinished Business in Latin America
articles.summary: “I want to get Cuba done before I leave you,” President Donald Trump told a conservative radio host on Nov. 12. It is a reminder that, despite the historic beating his party took in the midterm elections, Trump continues to see Latin America as a crucial part of his legacy. articles.title: Immigration Is Not a Fringe Issue
articles.summary: At a Senate forum on ICE violence, I listened to the sons of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo describe the morning their father was shot dead by ICE agents while on his way to work. Besides them sat and wept the families of Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti . Next to me were clergy wearing t-shirts that said “ Connected Americans ” and whispering prayers as they listened to the testimony of families whose loved ones had been killed in the streets. articles.title: Measles Is Back in the U.S. What Happens Next?
articles.summary: On Nov. 17, the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) declared that measles is no longer considered "eliminated" in the U.S. In the past year, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recorded more than 5,800 cases of measles—the highest caseload since 1991. Vaccination programs and increased monitoring of incoming measles cases helped the U.S. to eliminate measles in 2000, meaning there was no consistent spread of the virus within the country for more than a year. articles.title: This Moderate Democrat Thinks Trump Could Help Rein In ICE
articles.summary: Representative Henry Cuellar has been in Congress for more than 20 years, representing a South Texas district that includes a big chunk of Texas' border with Mexico. Over the years, he has fended off pressures from both parties: Democrats have tried and failed to replace him with someone more liberal; Republicans have tried and failed to convince him to join the GOP. articles.title: TIME's Top 100 Photos of 2026
articles.summary: In 2026, the earth was rocked by more extreme weather and the moon seemed once again within our reach. The streets of our cities were rushed by celebrating sports fans and thronged with angry citizens. Technological change, with all the fear and excitement it brings, seemed to accelerate faster than ever. People reached for greatness —or, in a time of global conflict , simply for peace.
